pour_patterns.name: Better 1 Cup
pour_patterns.creator: James Hoffmann
pour_patterns.description: A single cup in five equal pours: a 50 g bloom, then four 50 g pulses every 20 seconds, each a slow circular pour of about 5 g/s with the spout low. A gentle swirl after the bloom and after the last pour.

pour_patterns.name: Ultimate V60 Technique
pour_patterns.creator: James Hoffmann
pour_patterns.description: A bloom of twice the coffee's weight, swirled until evenly wet, then two continuous pours: to 60% of the water by 1:15, a little agitated, and to 100% by 1:45, slower and gentler. A stir each way and a final swirl flatten the bed.

temperature.note: as hot as possible for light roasts; for dark roasts waiting a little after the boil is fine

phases.note: slower and gentler, keep the cone topped up
stir once each way, drain a little, then swirl once; the video gives no target time

pour_patterns.name: 4:6 Method
pour_patterns.creator: Tetsu Kasuya
pour_patterns.description: Five pours of coarse coffee. The first 40% of the water, split in two, sets the balance of sweetness and acidity; the last 60%, split in three, sets the strength. The dripper comes off at 3:30.

phases.note: first 40%: a smaller first pour gives a sweeter cup
last 60%: more pours give a stronger cup

pour_patterns.name: One & Done
pour_patterns.creator: Lance Hedrick
pour_patterns.description: Two short wetting pours of 45 g each, then the rest of the water in one fast pour of about 10 g/s in small coin-sized circles in the centre. Grind so the brew finishes between 2:00 and 2:30.

phases.note: an optional small swirl adds 10 to 15 seconds if the grind is too coarse

pour_patterns.name: Easy & Effective V60
pour_patterns.creator: Lance Hedrick
pour_patterns.description: A pour every 30 seconds: two small blooms to 50 g and 100 g, each followed by a spin of the brewer, then two fast pours aimed just behind the centre to 220 g and 340 g, each followed by a swirl to level the bed.

pour_patterns.name: 1:2:1 Method
pour_patterns.creator: Lance Hedrick
pour_patterns.description: A long bloom of three times the coffee's weight, poured from high and from the outside in, then swirled hard. At 2:00 one main pour, heavy and high until the cone is half full, then lower and slower in small circles to the top. A shallow stir and small swirls keep the bed flat.

phases.note: heavy and high first, then lower and slower

pour_patterns.name: Rao Spin Method
pour_patterns.creator: Scott Rao
pour_patterns.description: A pre-wet of three times the coffee's weight, stirred so every ground is wet within about ten seconds, then one continuous pour at a steady height over the whole slurry. A single gentle stir and a spin of the brewer, the Rao spin, flatten the bed for an even drawdown.

phases.note: stir dry spots with a spoon
one continuous pour at one height
one gentle stir, then spin the brewer two to four turns

pour_patterns.name: April Brewing Method
pour_patterns.creator: April Coffee Roasters
pour_patterns.description: Two 100 g pours without a separate bloom, each starting with 30 g in a circle and finishing with 70 g in the centre, at about 10 g/s. Written for the flat-bottomed April Brewer.

pour_patterns.name: Neo Method
pour_patterns.creator: Tetsu Kasuya
pour_patterns.description: Published as The Neo Brew for the HARIO NEO dripper; a V60 also works. Extremely coarse coffee and ten 30 g pours: a bloom, then a pour every 15 seconds. Water should flow straight through rather than pool.

pour_patterns.name: Ultimate AeroPress Technique
pour_patterns.creator: James Hoffmann
pour_patterns.description: Brewed upright with no rinse or preheat. All the water goes on at once, the plunger goes in about 1 cm to stop the drip, and the coffee steeps for two minutes. A gentle swirl, 30 seconds to settle, then a gentle press all the way.

temperature.note: for light roasts; for darker roasts use more coffee and a coarser grind

phases.note: wet all the coffee while pouring
plunger in about 1 cm to stop the drip
gently, all the way; the recipe gives no press time

pour_patterns.name: Basic AeroPress Recipe
pour_patterns.creator: Tim Wendelboe
pour_patterns.description: A filter-style cup: light-roast coffee ground fine for filter, boiling water, three stirs, a 60-second steep under the plunger, three more stirs back to front, then a firm press with body weight without over-pressing.

phases.note: plunger on to stop the drip
plunger off, stir 3 times back to front
with body weight, don't over-press; the recipe gives no press time

pour_patterns.name: April AeroPress Recipe
pour_patterns.creator: April Coffee Roasters
pour_patterns.description: Two fast pours: 50 g stirred to agitate, then the remaining 150 g at 0:30. The press starts at 1:30 and the brew is done at 2:00. Written for bright Kenyan and Ethiopian coffees.

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2009
pour_patterns.creator: Łukasz Jura
pour_patterns.description: About 50 g of water and a few controlled stirs wet all the coarse grounds, then the rest of the water goes on. Pressing starts at 2:05 and takes 15 seconds.

phases.note: stir 4, 6 or 8 times until all grounds are wet

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2013
pour_patterns.creator: Jeff Verellen
pour_patterns.description: A 40-second bloom with 50 g of water, the remaining 220 g slightly cooler, then a slow 30-second press that leaves about 50 g of water and coffee in the brewer.

phases.note: slowly; leave about 50 g in the brewer

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2014
pour_patterns.creator: Shuichi Sasaki
pour_patterns.description: A 40 g bloom of 25 seconds and five stirs, the remaining 210 g with one stir, then a very slow 75-second press that leaves 45 g of slurry in the brewer. Low water temperature.

phases.note: very slowly; leave 45 g of slurry in the brewer

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2015
pour_patterns.creator: Lukáš Zahradník
pour_patterns.description: Finely ground coffee, 60 g of water and 15 seconds of agitation, then the remaining 200 g and a press that starts right away. Pressing stops just below the 1 mark, so not all the water goes through; about 2 minutes in total.

phases.note: start right away; stop just below the 1 mark

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2016
pour_patterns.creator: Filip Kucharczyk
pour_patterns.description: A strong concentrate of very coarse coffee: 150 g of water in about 15 seconds, 20 seconds of vigorous stirring, a couple more stirs at 1:00, then a gentle press done around 1:30. Diluted with 100 to 150 g of water to taste.

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2017
pour_patterns.creator: Paulina Miczka
pour_patterns.description: A concentrate of coffee ground as for a V60: 150 g of water mixed for 20 seconds, pressing from 1:05 to 1:35, then 150 to 200 g of water from the same kettle.

phases.note: mix with a stirrer or the back of a spoon

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2018
pour_patterns.creator: Carolina Ibarra Garay
pour_patterns.description: A very strong brew of finely ground coffee through two rinsed paper filters: 100 g of water poured over 30 seconds, 30 seconds of clockwise stirring and a 30-second press past the hiss. Topped up with 60 g of hot and 40 g of room-temperature water.

phases.note: stir clockwise without touching the filters
with forearm and body weight, past the hiss

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2019
pour_patterns.creator: Wendelien van Bunnik
pour_patterns.description: A bright concentrate: 100 g of water on coffee ground like table sugar, ten circular stirs, the plunger on, and a gentle press after 45 seconds. Diluted with 100 to 120 g of hot water; darker roasts want cooler water.

phases.note: gently; the recipe gives no press time

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2021
pour_patterns.creator: Tuomas Merikanto
pour_patterns.description: Coarse coffee through two paper filters: all the water at once, three gentle stirs, a steep to 1:30, three more stirs, then the plunger on and a press from 1:40 to 2:00. Low water temperature.

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2022
pour_patterns.creator: Jibbi Little
pour_patterns.description: Coffee ground twice and sifted, brewed with 94 g of water and 12 gentle stirs, pressed at 1:30 onto 20 g of cold water in the server, then topped up with hot water to 150 g.

phases.note: gently; the recipe gives no press time

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2024
pour_patterns.creator: George Stanica
pour_patterns.description: Two rinsed paper filters. A 50 g bloom of 30 seconds, water to 225 g, a gentle north-south-east-west stir for 10 seconds, then a slow 40-second press from 1:30. Diluted with 15 to 30 g of room-temperature water and left to cool for a few minutes.

pour_patterns.name: World AeroPress Champion 2025
pour_patterns.creator: Nemo Pop
pour_patterns.description: Sifted coffee through two paper filters, pressed into a carafe that already holds 70 g of bypass water at 50 °C. 100 g of brew water, a north-south then west-east stir at 0:25, and a gentle 20-second press from 0:50.

pour_patterns.name: Bloom
pour_patterns.description: A small first pour, about two to three times the coffee's weight, wets all the grounds; a rest of 30 to 45 seconds lets carbon dioxide escape before the main pours.

pour_patterns.name: Continuous pour
pour_patterns.description: After the bloom, all remaining water goes on in one uninterrupted pour, keeping the slurry level steady until the kettle is empty.

pour_patterns.name: Pulse pouring
pour_patterns.description: The water goes on in several separate pours with pauses between them, so the slurry level rises and falls and each pour agitates the bed again.

pour_patterns.name: Stepped flow
pour_patterns.description: One continuous pour whose rate changes in distinct steps, for example fast to raise the slurry and then slow to hold its level.

pour_patterns.name: Constant flow
pour_patterns.description: The kettle keeps one fixed flow rate, for example 5 grams per second, for the whole pour, which makes the brew easy to repeat.

pour_patterns.name: Ramp-up flow
pour_patterns.description: The pour starts gently and gets faster, so the bed is wetted calmly before agitation and slurry height increase.

pour_patterns.name: Ramp-down flow
pour_patterns.description: The pour starts fast to lift and mix the bed and slows down towards the end, so the bed settles flat before the drawdown.

pour_patterns.name: Variable flow
pour_patterns.description: The flow rate changes freely over the pour, faster and slower as the brewer chooses, rather than following one simple shape.

pour_patterns.name: Freeform reference replay
pour_patterns.description: A previously recorded pour, for example from a smart scale, is followed as a target curve so another brewer or another day can reproduce it.

pour_patterns.name: Osmotic flow
pour_patterns.description: A slow, gentle pour, usually in the centre, that lets water spread through the bed with little agitation instead of churning it.

pour_patterns.name: Double bloom
pour_patterns.description: Two separate wetting pours with rests before the main pours, to degas very fresh coffee or reach every dry pocket of the bed.

pour_patterns.name: Pulse flow drill
pour_patterns.description: A pouring exercise rather than a brew: one 48-second pour whose flow swings smoothly between about 2 and 6 g/s every 12 seconds, to practise speeding up and easing off the kettle without stopping.

pour_patterns.name: Stepped flow drill
pour_patterns.description: A pouring exercise rather than a brew: one 74-second pour that climbs in steps of 2 g/s from 2 to 10 g/s and back down, holding each rate for 6 seconds, to practise pouring at a steady chosen flow.

pour_patterns.name: Immersion
pour_patterns.description: All the water goes on at once and the coffee steeps in it, usually with a stir, before the brew is separated from the grounds, for example by pressing it through the filter of an AeroPress.

pour_patterns.name: Center pour
pour_patterns.description: The stream stays in the middle of the bed, which keeps agitation low and the bed shape steady.

pour_patterns.name: Circular pour
pour_patterns.description: The kettle moves in small circles around the middle, wetting more of the bed than a centre pour without reaching the paper.

pour_patterns.name: Spiral pour
pour_patterns.description: The stream moves progressively outward from the centre and back in, wetting the whole bed evenly.

pour_patterns.name: Back-and-forth pour
pour_patterns.description: The stream sweeps across the bed from side to side, turning over the grounds along its line.

pour_patterns.name: Hybrid movement
pour_patterns.description: The kettle switches between movements within one brew, for example small circles first and then a centre pour.

pour_patterns.name: Fixed-point pour
pour_patterns.description: The stream is held at one chosen position off the centre, for example to push the slurry in one direction or rinse one side of the paper.
